target_customer: Consumers buying bubble tea from a self-serve machine, initially MIT dorm residents, with venues as possible hosts
problem: Bubble tea needs staff and a shop; the founders built a refrigerator style dispenser that vends drinks after an app payment.
business_model: Hardware dispenser selling drinks per cup through an app payment

founders.name: Catherine Zeng
previous_startups: Earlier contracting work marketplace idea funded by MIT Sandbox (abandoned)
founders.background_notes: YC page bio says she is working on niknak.com. Education from MIT admissions blog post of 2017-12-04.

founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no bio there.

founders.background_notes: Named as a creator in the MIT blog post but not on the YC page, so the co-founder status is unconfirmed.

technical_complexity.rationale: The prototype was a refrigerator with a tablet, an Arduino and an AWS backend, which a student team could build; reliable food handling hardware at scale would be harder.

defensibility.rationale: A fridge with a tablet and payment app had no stated patents, data or contracts, so it was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent acting against it; the company simply went inactive.

market_need_then: Bubble tea was popular with students and the MIT post describes dorm demand, but no spending or customer figures are public.

branding.domain_note: Used lambdatea.com; no acquisition history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: YC tagline is playful, ending in an emoticon

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community material about the brand was found beyond a student blog post and directory listings.

pivots.from: Marketplace for contracting work funded by MIT Sandbox
pivots.why: The MIT blog says the team did not believe enough in the first idea to follow up

outcome_analysis: Lambda Tea was an MIT student team that pivoted from a contracting marketplace to a boba vending machine and joined YC in Winter 2018. The company site returned an error and YC lists it as inactive, but no shutdown notice or post-mortem is public, so the cause of failure is not public. Nothing about funding, customers or machine deployments was found.
notes: Company site lambdatea.com returned HTTP 503 on fetch. Dealroom lists it as closed with an HQ that does not match MIT, so treat with caution. No dated competitor found near the batch; later automated boba players (Bobacino, Let's Tea) lack dated sources. Cause of failure is not public; failure_factors other is a placeholder meaning unspecified.
